# Training pack: Build an executive assistant agent

**Use case.** Build an executive assistant agent that helps me manage email, calendar, meetings, follow-ups and briefings.

**Outcome.** A personal assistant agent that triages your inbox, drafts replies in your style, proposes meeting times, prepares briefing notes before meetings, tracks follow-ups and actions, and remembers your preferences. It acts only with your approval, under access controls you set. You will also know when a ready-made assistant in your existing tools is the better choice.

**Assumptions**

- You are willing to learn or refresh basic Python, or will use the low-code Microsoft route in capability 5.
- Your email, calendar and documents live in Google Workspace or Microsoft 365.
- The agent drafts and proposes; you approve anything sent, accepted or deleted, at least until it has proved reliable.

Pack last updated 2026-10-22. Hours and costs come from the database dated 2026-10-22; EUR conversions use the European Central Bank euro foreign exchange reference rates dated 2026-10-21. Totals add only published figures. Anything not published or not verified is listed separately, so the totals are a floor, not a quote.

## 7. Secure it against untrusted content

Every incoming email is untrusted input. A malicious message can try to make the assistant leak data or take actions (prompt injection), so access and actions must be tightly limited.

## Build milestones

Apply each capability as you go. Each milestone produces evidence you can show.

| # | Milestone | After capability | What you produce |
|---:|---|---|---|
| 1 | Write the assistant's job description | 1 | One-page spec: which tasks it does alone, drafts for approval, or never touches; the tone it writes in; who it may contact; what it may read. |
| 2 | Inbox triage on exported mail | 3 | A script that sorts a sample of your exported email into act, delegate, read later and ignore, extracts actions and deadlines, and drafts replies in your style. No live access yet. |
| 3 | Memory of you | 4 | Stored preferences, key contacts and standing rules that the assistant uses and updates, for example meeting-time preferences and who gets priority. |
| 4 | Read-only live connection | 5, 7 | The assistant reads your mailbox and calendar with the narrowest permissions available, cannot send or delete, and passes your own prompt-injection tests. |
| 5 | Daily briefing | 6 | Each morning: today's meetings with a briefing note per meeting (who, history, open items, sources), urgent emails, and overdue follow-ups. |
| 6 | Supervised actions and pilot | 8, 9 | Drafts and calendar proposals that you approve with one click, an audit log, a privacy note, accuracy measured over two weeks, and a buy-versus-build comparison with the assistants built into Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace. |

## To research next

- Courses on the Gmail, Google Calendar and Microsoft Graph APIs, and OAuth scopes for assistants.
- Training on securing tool-using agents against prompt injection (least privilege, approval gates).
- GDPR and data-protection training for AI assistants, preferably from Irish or EU bodies.
- Google Workspace (Gemini) and Microsoft 365 Copilot agent-building training, to compare buy with build.
- Deploying and scheduling small agents with course-specific evidence.

## Notes

- The AI project manager pack shares several capabilities (LLM API, agents, MCP, retrieval). Training taken for one counts for the other.
- Your email and calendar provider probably already offers a built-in assistant. Compare it with your milestone 1 spec before building everything yourself.
- Keep the assistant read-only and draft-only until testing shows it is reliable and resistant to prompt injection.
